title: Progressive chunk assembly and backfill protocol for structured streams
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We frequently receive truncated or partially-escaped structured output from streaming LLM responses when network glitches, model truncation, or connector timeouts occur. Existing approaches (simple rejoin-on-boundary, naive JSON repair) either lose fidelity or enable unsound tool invocations. Goal: define a progressive chunk assembly and backfill protocol that allows the runtime + SDKs to: 1) safely assemble fragments into valid JSON where possible, 2) mark and surface irrecoverable truncations explicitly, 3) enable idempotent retries without double-applying tool calls, and 4) provide a compatibility shim for legacy clients that expect delta frames or plain-text deltas.

Protocol overview (high-level):
- Chunk manifest header: every stream MAY start with an optional manifest frame that advertises stream_id, first_seq, window_hints, and a manifest_checksum. This is optional to keep backward compatibility with older clients.
- Chunk frames: each data frame includes metadata as text prefixes (human-readable, newline delimited) in the form: CHUNK-ID:<uuid> SEQ:<n> TYPE:<complete|prefix|suffix|mid> LEN:<bytes> CHECKSUM:<sha1> RETRY-TOKEN:<base64>
- Fragment semantics:
  - complete: contains a full self-contained JSON value (no assembly required).
  - prefix: starts a JSON structure but ends mid-structure (no closing brace/array end).
  - suffix: completes a previously started prefix/mid chain.
  - mid: a middle fragment between prefix and suffix.
- Assembly rules:
  1) Use SEQ ordering to coalesce fragments for a given CHUNK-ID. If fragments are missing, attempt backfill using RETRY-TOKEN to request retransmit from the server; server will attempt to provide missing SEQ frames for up to a configured window (default 5s or 3 retransmit attempts).
  2) Once assembled, validate against a permissive JSON parser that accepts single top-level value and tolerant trailing commas. If validation fails, run a lightweight heuristic pass that (a) balances curly/bracket counts, (b) inspects string literal boundaries to avoid accidental join inside strings, and (c) tries to inject minimal backfill markers ("__BACKFILL_PLACEHOLDER__") only where JSON structure is unambiguously broken.
  3) If heuristics succeed, mark produced document with metadata: assembled: true, backfilled: true, backfill_strategy: <heuristic|gap-retransmit>. If heuristics fail, produce a deterministic failure payload and surface a clear error to the SDK: {"error_type":"TRUNCATED_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT","partial_text":"<...>","retry_token":"<token>"}.

Tool/function-calling semantics:
- Tool calls must be guarded by idempotency tokens produced by the runtime before emitting the first fragment that contains the tool call marker. The token is included in the frame metadata as CALL-ID:<uuid>. On retry, the runtime will avoid re-executing the same CALL-ID unless the upstream caller explicitly requests forced re-run.
- For legacy clients that cannot parse CALL-ID, the runtime will emit an additional idempotency hint in plain text logs and surface a best-effort deduplication window on serverside (30s).

Compatibility layer:
- SDKs: new SDKs will parse the manifest and chunk prefixes automatically. Older SDKs will continue to receive delta frames; server will map deltas to chunk frames and include a compatibility envelope: LEGACY-SEQUENCE:<n> LEGACY-MODE:delta. We will publish a lightweight polyfill (npm + pypi) so customers can adopt without server rollouts.

Retries and failure modes:
- Retries use RETRY-TOKEN that encodes stream_id, last_seq_seen, and a short HMAC. Retry requests are idempotent and limited to the manifest window. Retries beyond the window produce TRUNCATED_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT and an explicit SLA-exempt flag for the request so callers can make deterministic decisions.
- When a tool call is present and the stream is truncated before the tool-call response, the SDK surfaces a special state "tool_call_pending_truncation" and exposes the CALL-ID so orchestrators can re-request the tool output via a managed re-run API instead of re-invoking the external tool directly.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict assembly + blocking retransmit improves fidelity but increases tail latency for streaming-first UX. We chose a hybrid: optimistic assembly + background backfill; immediate best-effort heuristics for UX, but a deterministic TRUNCATION response if heuristics fail.
- Injecting placeholders preserves parseability but leaks a synthetic token into structured output; therefore placeholders are opt-in by default and require review for downstream consumers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests covering assembly, heuristic backfill, malformed unicode and escaped-quote edge cases.
- Integration test: end-to-end with SDK polyfill, simulating missing frames and verifying deterministic error payloads and retry behavior.
- Benchmark: median additional latency for successful assembly < 12ms; P99 < 220ms for backfill window under normal load.
- Documentation: Confluence spec + SDK migration guide + breaking-change notice for legacy clients.

Artifacts:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood-internal.local/display/INF/Progressive+Chunk+Assembly+Spec
- Draft runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892
- SDK polyfill package (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-polyfills/tree/stream-chunk-assembly

Next steps:
- Finish runtime wiring for chunk prefixes and retry-token HMAC (ENG owner: Marco)
- Publish SDK polyfill alpha and run canary with internal tools team
- Add observability metrics: fragment_retransmit_rate, assembly_success_rate, truncated_stream_count
